text:
elaine: Quick update from the latency-bounty sprint — short summary first: p50 ~0% (unchanged), p95 -9%, p99 -22%, estimated token cost down ~11% for the web-tier on gpt-small-v1. :tada:

elaine: What changed: we shipped the "early-exit token collapse" heuristic + lightweight input trimming at the proxy. The heuristic detects high-prob prefix completions and short-circuits further decoding when top-k mass > 0.995 for three consecutive steps. Also a tiny change to call-site: drop redundant system prompt chunking for single-turn queries (saves ~6 tokens avg).

elaine: Canary started at 08:07 UTC on two GPUs (tag: runtime/earlyexit-trim/v1). Bench harness: synthetic tail-heavy traces + a sampled 1% production traffic replay.

tim: Nice. Any quality regressions caught in evals?

elaine: We ran our prompt-set evals (chat sims + a random 10k queries). No meaningful drop in top-1 accuracy on the monitored prompts. A handful of edge cases where a very long greedy prefix ended early; we added a safety floor by requiring min_decodes=6 for any response < 64 tokens.

jonah: Do you have the raw numbers from the canary? p50/p95/p99 plus token cost?

elaine: Paste from bench run: 
```
baseline (tag=runtime/main): p50 34ms, p95 112ms, p99 378ms, token-cpu-cost=1.00
canary  (earlyexit-trim/v1): p50 33ms, p95 102ms, p99 296ms, token-cpu-cost=0.89
diff: p95 -9ms (-8%), p99 -82ms (-21.7%), cost -11%
```

priya: That's a solid tail win. Where did the p99 improvements actually come from — fewer KV cache misses, less decode time, or shorter avg seq?

elaine: Mostly fewer decode steps: for tail-heavy traces we reduced average decode length by ~12% because of early exits. Small reduction in KV read rate (prefix collapse reduces KV churn for long contexts). No infra-level changes besides the canary config.

jonah: Any infra gotchas? Memory, scheduling, or batching regressions?

elaine: Observed slightly higher microbatch variance during the first 30m of canary as the runtime adapted to shorter sequences (batcher coalescence changed), but scheduler adjustments smoothed it out. No OOMs. We throttled the canary to 2% traffic for first hour and increased to 10% after sanity checks.

infra-bot: deploy: runtime/earlyexit-trim/v1 -> canary on pool-gpu-a (2 instances) at 2024-10-12T08:07:12Z

priya: Are we going to roll this to production? Any feature flags?

elaine: Plan is gradual flip: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours, with automatic rollback if p99 increases or eval regressions > 1%. Feature flag: "runtime.early_exit.enabled" (defaults to true for canary). We also added "runtime.early_exit.min_decodes" and "runtime.early_exit.topk_mass" for knobbing.

tim: Can you drop the rollout commands here so the ops oncall can follow?

elaine: Sure — rollout script we used: 
```
# canary
redwood deploy set-tag --pool pool-gpu-a --tag runtime/earlyexit-trim/v1 --pct 2
sleep 3600
redwood deploy set-tag --pool pool-gpu-a --tag runtime/earlyexit-trim/v1 --pct 10
# increase to 50% after 6h if metrics stable
```

jonah: Nice, please add a short post to #eng-notices and cc product so they can update the docs (noting token savings). Also add the eval artifacts to the benchmark bucket.

elaine: Will do. I've uploaded the eval CSVs to s3://ci-redwood/benchmarks/earlyexit-trim/v1 and created a quicknote in Confluence (link below).

elaine: Known limitations: not appropriate for streaming multi-tool calls (we disable early-exit for streams) and for prompts that include "do not stop" style instructions (we treat those as opt-outs).

priya: Any reason not to backport to dedicated clusters? Some customers on Dedicated might prefer the cost savings but also want determinism.

elaine: We added a dedicated toggle and will only enable on a per-customer consent basis. Product owns outreach.

tim: Thanks team. Big win for tail latency. Small ask — can we add a quick metric to the console showing "avg decoded tokens per request" per model? Helps quantify wins in the future.

elaine: On it. I'll file a console feature ticket and ping devex.

priya: :rocket: congrats and thx for quick iteration.

jonah: :thumbsup:

elaine: Closing thread with the rollout timeline: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours, rollback conditions in place. Will post a short runbook to #eng-ops once 50% stable.
